title: The Voice That Stops the Knife

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then he reached out his hand and took the knife to slay his son. But the angel of the Lord called out to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied. - Gen 22:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The knife is raised. Abraham has proven his heart is fully surrendered - and at that very instant, heaven breaks in: "Abraham! Abraham!" God stops him. The test is complete; the sacrifice of Isaac was never God's true intention. At the last possible moment, the voice from heaven halts the knife.

Notice the urgency and tenderness of the double call - "Abraham! Abraham!" It is the cry of a God who was watching every second, who had never intended for Isaac to die, and who intervenes at exactly the right moment. God was present through the whole ordeal, and His timing was perfect.

There is deep comfort here. God sees the very edge of our trials. He knows exactly how far we are being stretched, and He is never late. Abraham had walked all the way to the knife-raised moment, and God met him there. Sometimes deliverance comes at the last instant - but it comes.

And once again, notice Abraham's answer: "Here I am." The same words as when the test began (v.1). Through the whole agonising journey, Abraham remained available, attentive, ready to hear God's voice - even now, ready to be stopped as readily as he had been ready to obey. May we too keep our hearts so tuned to God that, whether He calls us to act or to stop, we are always saying, "Here I am." The God who watched over Abraham watches over you, and He is never late.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you trust that God sees the very edge of your trials and is never late?
- Is your heart tuned to hear God, ready to act or to stop at His word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You see the edge of my trials and are never late. Keep my heart so tuned to Your voice that whether You call me to act or to stop, I am always ready to say, "Here I am."
Amen.
